trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out down, up, right or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down.
Going left would force the line onto number 4 before its turn. So the line goes right.
Going up would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So the line goes right.
The line must go up: right is number 6, which comes later.

Going left, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,5); going to number 3 would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So the line goes right.

The line must go up: left is number 5, which comes later.
Cell (2,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
Cell (2,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Going left, the next 5 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,1). So the line goes down.
Cell (4,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going up, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,2). So the line goes down.
Going right would leave both cell (4,2) and cell (6,2) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Cell (3,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Cell (1,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
